How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

Figures and the rules behind them **Important:** every figure on the screen is calculated **in the browser**, mostly in `features/rates/rates.ts`. A clerk's settle above the clerk limit becomes `PENDING`, which a steward approves (`SETTLED`) or rejects (back to `OPEN`). `VOID` is final. `DELETED` applies to drafts only. | | `claim-number` | `number` | Given on **open** by `ClaimNumbers.next`: `FY-n`, counted across the sheet's whole tree, within the fiscal year the claim's **due-by** falls in (`fiscalStartMonth`). Once `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, numbers run per period instead: `-n`, or `X-n` outside any period. Numbers are never reused. A voided claim keeps its number. A reassigned or transferred claim gets a new one. | | `claim-due-by` | `dueBy` | `NewDueBy`: the *terms*-th business day after the claim date, skipping weekends and holidays. Terms come from the person's own terms, else the grade's (`terms-`), else the sheet's (default 14), each as in force on the claim date. Fixed at creation. A re-date keeps it, an edit keeps it, and a split gets a fresh one. **But** adding a holiday re-fixes it (`RefixDueBys`) for every claim that isn't SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday. | | `claim-due` | `claimDue` / `Claim.due` | If settled, the frozen `due`. Otherwise `max(floorOn(date), figure + lateCharge)`. **figure** is the statement-bound `statedDue` when `bound()` (stated and not PENDING), else `amount × rate / 100`. The rate is `Rate.inForce` for the person's `gradeOn(date)` on the claim date, falling back to the parent sheet's rates; with no rate the figure is `n/a`. A correction gets no floor and no late charge. | | (rounding) | `Rounding.modeFor` / `roundingFor` | HALF_UP if the claim date is before `policyDate`, otherwise HALF_EVEN. A blank policy date means the **sheet's today**. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. | | (late charge) | `LateCharge.on` / `lateCharge` | Compounding. For each full 30 days past `dueBy + grace-`, it adds `latePctOn(boundary)` × (figure + earlier charges). A boundary at 0.00 adds nothing. Never charged on corrections or deferred claims. Never bound by a statement. | | `claim-overdue` | `overdue` | OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy + grace` is before today. | | `claim-deferred`, `-until` | `deferred(today)` | OPEN and today < `deferredUntil`. It is `n/a` when the grade in force today has no rate today **and** no counting claim has any figure. - `person-excess`: how far the sum is above the cap (0.00 if not above, or if n/a). - `person-overdue-count` / `-total`: counting claims that are overdue, and their dues (late charges included). Not capped. - `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` (`personSplit`): counting dues split into SETTLED versus OPEN/PENDING. Not capped. - `person-aged-0-30|31-60|61`: dues of counting OPEN/PENDING claims, bucketed by days from the claim date to today. - `person-active`: has a counting OPEN/PENDING claim dated in the 30 days up to today. - `person-period-

A tag total counts a claim that has the tag itself or whose person has it. - `my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total`: the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user. - `consolidated-*`: this sheet plus all descendant sheets, each sheet's own trimmed totals added up. - `summary-grade--count|due-total|active`: retired people excluded. `summary-period-

-due-total|change`: change compared with the previous period by start date. `summary-status--count`, `summary-void--count`, `header-people-count` (includes retired people). - `rate-preview-count|diff`: how many OPEN/PENDING claims would change due under a candidate rate, and the total change. - `plan-generated-count`, `plan-next-dates`, `pool-total-share`, `pool-balanced`, `pool-cut`, `period-due-total` (frozen `closedTotal` once closed). ### Who may do what - **Viewer**: no changes at all (`CheckNotViewer` runs first in every write pipeline). **Archived sheet**: no changes (`CheckNotArchived`). - **Permission matrix** (`Permissions`): open, settle, void and close default to clerk + steward. Reassign and reopen default to steward. Split needs the "open" permission. - **Steward only, fixed in code**: approve and reject (reject needs a reason), re-settle, voiding a SETTLED claim (only within 7 days of the last SETTLED log date), re-date, cancelling a statement, transfer, merge. A `Delegation` in force on today makes a user act as a steward. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim can't settle or approve it, and neither can its last editor (`editedBy`). - **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above `clerkLimitOn` makes it PENDING instead. - **Proof threshold** (the grade's own, else the sheet's): with 0 proofs, settle and approve are refused. Changing today also writes SNAPSHOT lines, records the sheet day, unlocks all editors and auto-closes any period whose to-date plus `graceDays` is before the new today. - **Entry date**: when set, a claim left blank takes it instead of today. - Dated settings (`DatedSettings`): the value in force is the one with the latest from-date on or before the date. Defaults are floor 1.00, late percent 0.00 and terms 14. ### Statements, holds, retirement, closed periods, imports - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): binds each counting claim to its *figure*, meaning the rate only, without floor or late charge. It unbinds the rest and records `statedTotal`, which is capped and includes floor and late charge. "As of" a date replays the sheet as it stood that day. A split or reassign drops a claim's binding. Cancelling unbinds all claims and goes back to the previous statement's total. - **Hold**: removes covered OPEN/PENDING, unbound claims from every live total and gives the person 0.00 pool cuts. It blocks no actions. - **Retirement**: claims dated after the retirement date are refused (add, reassign to the person, re-date, paste, plans). A past retirement refuses dates strictly inside it. Retired people can't be transferred or merged. - **Closed period** (by due-by): every change to its claims is refused, and so is adding a claim whose due-by would fall in it. Its totals are frozen. **Soft-close** freezes the totals but still allows changes; new claims are flagged as late entries. **Reopen** makes the totals live again. - **Imports and bulk adds**: - People import: a line matching an existing name or alias updates that person (grade recorded from today; terms and contact only if given). Otherwise it adds a person. - Rate import: replaces any rate with the same grade and from-date. - Paste: adds DRAFT claims; no corrections; a trailing ` #ref` becomes the reference. - Quick add: creates a new person at grade A if the name is unknown. - Plans: add DRAFTs up to the earlier of the plan's end and today; a refused date is skipped and retried next time. Imports, paste and quick add are all-or-nothing. - **Audit**: ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines (`RollupLines`) follow most changes. ALERT is written when a person's due-total crosses `alertThreshold`. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard. Each piece is well commented, but the logic is scattered and duplicated: - **Two copies of the due math.** The same rules exist in Java and TypeScript. Totals are built separately in about 4 server places and about 15 React components. - **Rules are split up.** Business checks live in roughly 100 single-method step classes, and which checks apply to an action is only visible in the YAML pipelines. - **Comments disagree with the code.** I found at least five cases: - Docs say due-by never changes after creation, but adding a holiday re-fixes it. - Docs say "sheet-wide numbers 1, 2…", but numbers are now `FY-n`. - `PeriodCloser` and `ClaimLateEntry` say "dated in" a period, but the code uses due-by. - A settled claim voided after its period ended is dropped from the period total in Java (`Period.counts`) but still counted on screen (`countsInPeriod`). - "Cap" means two different things: a person's due-total cap and a period's open-claim cap. "Grace" also has two meanings: per-grade grace days for overdue, and sheet `graceDays` for auto-closing periods. A new developer would need to read both stacks side by side to trust any figure.

A pool pays out only when its shares total exactly 100.00 and there is a pot. Each cut is pot × share / (sum of shares that get a cut), rounded half-even. Retired or held members get 0.00, and the remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut. Members whose dates exclude today are left out. - `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`, `person-grade` (`gradeOn(today)`), `person-terms`, `person-retired(-from)`, `person-hold-line`, `person-clashing`, `person-origin`: as stored. ### Sheet totals - `rollup-claimed-total`: everyone's claimed, summed. - `rollup-due-total` and `rollup-overdue-total` (`trimmedTotal`): people's figures summed, skipping n/a, and **dropping the single highest and lowest** when there are three or more. `header-due-total` and `header-overdue-total` use the same rule. - `rollup-overdue-count`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, `rollup-cut-total`, `month--due-total`, `tag--due-total`: plain sums, not trimmed and not capped. A tag total counts a claim that has the tag itself or whose person has it. - `my-due-total` / `my-overdue-total`: the person whose name or alias matches the signed-in user. - `consolidated-*`: this sheet plus all descendant sheets, each sheet's own trimmed totals added up. - `summary-grade--count|due-total|active`: retired people excluded. `summary-period-

-due-total|change`: change compared with the previous period by start date. `summary-status--count`, `summary-void--count`, `header-people-count` (includes retired people). - `rate-preview-count|diff`: how many OPEN/PENDING claims would change due under a candidate rate, and the total change. - `plan-generated-count`, `plan-next-dates`, `pool-total-share`, `pool-balanced`, `pool-cut`, `period-due-total` (frozen `closedTotal` once closed). ### Who may do what - **Viewer**: no changes at all (`CheckNotViewer` runs first in every write pipeline). **Archived sheet**: no changes (`CheckNotArchived`). - **Permission matrix** (`Permissions`): open, settle, void and close default to clerk + steward. Reassign and reopen default to steward. Split needs the "open" permission. - **Steward only, fixed in code**: approve and reject (reject needs a reason), re-settle, voiding a SETTLED claim (only within 7 days of the last SETTLED log date), re-date, cancelling a statement, transfer, merge. A `Delegation` in force on today makes a user act as a steward. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim can't settle or approve it, and neither can its last editor (`editedBy`). - **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above `clerkLimitOn` makes it PENDING instead. - **Proof threshold** (the grade's own, else the sheet's): with 0 proofs, settle and approve are refused. This is checked before the clerk limit. - **Note threshold**: opening a claim with an empty note is refused when its due is above the threshold. - **Period cap**: opening is refused once the person already has `cap` OPEN/PENDING claims due in that period. - **Void reasons**: when the sheet has a list, a void must pick one of them. - **Restore**: a deleted claim can only be restored on the same "today" it was deleted. **Remind**: once per today, OPEN/PENDING only. **Edit**: DRAFT only, and not while another user's editor lock is on it. **Lines**: a claim with lines takes its amount from them. ### What a date decides - **Claim date** decides: grade, rate, floor, terms, grace, proof and note thresholds, rounding mode, hold coverage, the retirement refusal, the month bucket, the age, the active window and the backing window. - **Due-by** decides: the period, the number sequence, overdue status and late-charge boundaries, closed-period refusals, late entry and the period cap. - **Today** decides: the n/a test, the cap, deferral, overdue status, late charge, whether retirement has been reached, delegations, and auto-close. Changing today also writes SNAPSHOT lines, records the sheet day, unlocks all editors and auto-closes any period whose to-date plus `graceDays` is before the new today. - **Entry date**: when set, a claim left blank takes it instead of today. - Dated settings (`DatedSettings`): the value in force is the one with the latest from-date on or before the date. Defaults are floor 1.00, late percent 0.00 and terms 14. ### Statements, holds, retirement, closed periods, imports - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): binds each counting claim to its *figure*, meaning the rate only, without floor or late charge. It unbinds the rest and records `statedTotal`, which is capped and includes floor and late charge. "As of" a date replays the sheet as it stood that day. A split or reassign drops a claim's binding. Cancelling unbinds all claims and goes back to the previous statement's total. - **Hold**: removes covered OPEN/PENDING, unbound claims from every live total and gives the person 0.00 pool cuts. It blocks no actions. - **Retirement**: claims dated after the retirement date are refused (add, reassign to the person, re-date, paste, plans). A past retirement refuses dates strictly inside it. Retired people can't be transferred or merged. - **Closed period** (by due-by): every change to its claims is refused, and so is adding a claim whose due-by would fall in it. Its totals are frozen. **Soft-close** freezes the totals but still allows changes; new claims are flagged as late entries. **Reopen** makes the totals live again. - **Imports and bulk adds**: - People import: a line matching an existing name or alias updates that person (grade recorded from today; terms and contact only if given). Otherwise it adds a person. - Rate import: replaces any rate with the same grade and from-date. - Paste: adds DRAFT claims; no corrections; a trailing ` #ref` becomes the reference. - Quick add: creates a new person at grade A if the name is unknown. - Plans: add DRAFTs up to the earlier of the plan's end and today; a refused date is skipped and retried next time. Imports, paste and quick add are all-or-nothing. - **Audit**: ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines (`RollupLines`) follow most changes. ALERT is written when a person's due-total crosses `alertThreshold`. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard. Each piece is well commented, but the logic is scattered and duplicated: - **Two copies of the due math.** The same rules exist in Java and TypeScript. Totals are built separately in about 4 server places and about 15 React components. - **Rules are split up.** Business checks live in roughly 100 single-method step classes, and which checks apply to an action is only visible in the YAML pipelines. - **Comments disagree with the code.** I found at least five cases: - Docs say due-by never changes after creation, but adding a holiday re-fixes it. - Docs say "sheet-wide numbers 1, 2…", but numbers are now `FY-n`. - `PeriodCloser` and `ClaimLateEntry` say "dated in" a period, but the code uses due-by. - A settled claim voided after its period ended is dropped from the period total in Java (`Period.counts`) but still counted on screen (`countsInPeriod`). - "Cap" means two different things: a person's due-total cap and a period's open-claim cap. "Grace" also has two meanings: per-grade grace days for overdue, and sheet `graceDays` for auto-closing periods. A new developer would need to read both stacks side by side to trust any figure.
